topic-056-optimistic-online-mirror-desce.evolution: Early representatives develop online convex programming and no-regret gradients. Later work removes known-bound assumptions and addresses dynamic environments. Recent papers combine anytime constraints, parameter-free movement-aware analysis, and reductions for structured nonconvex objectives, extending online guarantees across feedback and feasibility settings.
openQuestions: Can adaptivity to unknown scales coexist with meaningful constraint guarantees?
How should regret account for delayed information and the cost of changing decisions?
topic-056-optimistic-online-mirror-desce.overview: Online optimization makes decisions before seeing each new loss, often while the environment or constraints change. This cluster studies regret guarantees for convex objectives, unbounded domains, adversarial constraints, delayed feedback, and movement costs. Adaptive algorithms seek competitive performance without requiring accurate advance knowledge of scales or variation.
topic-056-optimistic-online-mirror-desce.title: Adaptive Online Optimization and Dynamic Regret
topic-056-optimistic-online-mirror-desce.whyItMatters: A fixed comparator can hide failure when the best decision changes over time. Dynamic regret and explicit constraint control provide more relevant measures for systems that must keep adapting rather than converge to one permanent answer.

topic-057-a-block-coordinate-descent-app.evolution: The collection spans early sparse polynomial construction and regularized regression. Later work develops structured penalties, robust Lasso variants, and dual-gap screening. Recent examples address dependent time series and reuse sparse recovery for selecting interpretable editing directions, often pairing support selection with a separate debiasing step.
openQuestions: How should sparse selections reflect uncertainty among correlated alternatives?
Which screening guarantees extend to nonconvex penalties or dependent observations?
topic-057-a-block-coordinate-descent-app.overview: Sparse regression identifies a small set of useful coefficients, sometimes organized into groups or other structures. This topic develops penalties, optimization schemes, screening rules, and recovery guarantees for such models. Safe screening is a distinctive theme: it removes features only when they can be certified inactive at the optimum.
topic-057-a-block-coordinate-descent-app.title: Sparse Regression and Structured Regularization
topic-057-a-block-coordinate-descent-app.whyItMatters: Sparsity can improve interpretability and computation, but penalty choices can introduce bias and correlated features can complicate selection. Efficient algorithms need to distinguish provably unnecessary variables from those that merely look weak during early iterations.

topic-058-amag-additive-multiplicative-a.evolution: Earlier representatives concern temporal-difference networks and activity modeling. Later methods introduce recurrent graph distributions and continuous-time walks. Recent work integrates graph structure into state-space dynamics, explains temporal models through memory backtracking, and proves longitudinal stability for unfolded spectral embeddings under a dynamic block-model assumption.
openQuestions: How can temporal explanations distinguish persistent structure from a decisive transition?
Which stability guarantees survive abrupt changes and irregular observation times?
topic-058-amag-additive-multiplicative-a.overview: Temporal graphs combine changing connections with evolving node information. These papers study recurrent, state-space, spectral, and motif-based representations for that setting. They ask how to capture long-range temporal effects while preserving graph structure, and how to explain which past events or connections drive a prediction.
topic-058-amag-additive-multiplicative-a.title: Temporal Graph Representations and Dynamics
topic-058-amag-additive-multiplicative-a.whyItMatters: A useful dynamic embedding should change when the system changes, yet remain comparable across time. Without that balance, apparent motion in representation space can reflect the learning procedure rather than a meaningful event.

topic-059-a-cat-is-a-cat-not-a-dog-unrav.evolution: The collection begins with early zero-shot and diffusion-based text-to-image systems in 2021–2022. Later work improves semantic guidance and rectified-flow Transformers. Recent papers examine rare concepts, layer-specific erasure, and single-stream architectures, where shared text-image parameters make selective modification especially delicate.
openQuestions: How can concept removal be evaluated beyond a small set of prompts?
Which internal representations support precise semantic control without damaging unrelated content?
topic-059-a-cat-is-a-cat-not-a-dog-unrav.overview: Text-to-image diffusion models connect linguistic descriptions to visual generation through learned conditioning and denoising dynamics. This topic studies architecture, semantic guidance, text embeddings, scaling, and targeted concept modification. A recurring challenge is controlling one concept while preserving the model’s broader ability to generate coherent images.
topic-059-a-cat-is-a-cat-not-a-dog-unrav.title: Text-Conditioned Diffusion and Concept Control
topic-059-a-cat-is-a-cat-not-a-dog-unrav.whyItMatters: Strong average image quality can coexist with weak handling of rare semantics or unwanted memorization. Understanding where text and image information interact helps design changes that affect the intended content without collapsing generation.

topic-060-learning-to-branch-for-multi-t.evolution: Early representatives investigate learning many tasks with backpropagation and shared model bias. Later work develops flexible task clusters and feature sharing. Recent approaches learn which task combinations work well, analyze shared linear representations, and calibrate merged spectra to avoid counting overlapping directions repeatedly.
openQuestions: Can task compatibility be predicted without training every possible combination?
How should a merged model balance shared capabilities against rare task-specific behavior?
topic-060-learning-to-branch-for-multi-t.overview: Multi-task methods share information across objectives, either during joint training or by combining separately adapted models. This cluster studies task grouping, shared representations, asymmetric transfer, and weight-space merging. The central question is when sharing helps and when it creates interference or overemphasizes common structure.
topic-060-learning-to-branch-for-multi-t.title: Multi-Task Learning and Model Merging
topic-060-learning-to-branch-for-multi-t.whyItMatters: Related tasks are not automatically compatible at every layer or update direction. Good combinations need to account for both conflicting knowledge and repeated contributions from already shared components.

topic-061-neural-symbolic-regression-tha.evolution: Early representatives explore constituent structure in connectionist models. Later work develops differentiable theorem provers and SAT-based grounding. More recent methods learn proof-selection strategies, constrain neural inference with solvers, and design discrete architectures from which readable programs can be extracted, emphasizing both scalability and faithfulness.
openQuestions: How can extracted rules be tested beyond the examples used to learn them?
Which architectural biases make symbolic recovery easier without sacrificing useful flexibility?
topic-061-neural-symbolic-regression-tha.overview: Neurosymbolic methods combine learned representations with rules, constraints, or executable programs. These papers study differentiable proving, symbol grounding, satisfiability, and recovery of algorithms from trained networks. The goal is to obtain useful learning behavior while making some of the reasoning structure explicit and checkable.
topic-061-neural-symbolic-regression-tha.title: Neurosymbolic Reasoning and Algorithm Extraction
topic-061-neural-symbolic-regression-tha.whyItMatters: A correct answer may arise from a shortcut rather than the intended rule. Symbolic structure can support systematic generalization and explanations, but exhaustive proof search or poorly grounded symbols can make hybrid systems impractical.

topic-062-a-bayesian-framework-for-figur.evolution: Early examples use neural color segmentation and perceptual organization. The 2000s representatives develop shared probabilistic components, figure-ground cue integration, and contour models. Recent applications bring deformable anatomical priors and structure-preserving decompositions to medical segmentation, adapting the broader idea of coherent shape modeling to cross-domain data.
openQuestions: How can structural priors remain helpful when anatomy or object layout is atypical?
Which uncertainty measures reveal disagreement about object count or boundary placement?
topic-062-a-bayesian-framework-for-figur.overview: Segmentation and scene interpretation assign coherent regions, objects, and boundaries to visual input. This cluster combines spatial probabilistic models, grouping cues, multiscale fields, and structured priors. Rather than treating pixels independently, methods represent how parts and object instances fit together, sometimes with uncertainty about how many objects are present.
topic-062-a-bayesian-framework-for-figur.title: Scene Organization and Structure-Aware Segmentation
topic-062-a-bayesian-framework-for-figur.whyItMatters: Appearance varies across images and domains, while spatial or anatomical relationships can remain more stable. Incorporating that structure can reduce annotation needs and prevent locally plausible predictions from forming globally inconsistent shapes.

topic-063-a-framework-for-bayesian-optim.evolution: The collection begins with foundational GP regression and heteroscedastic models in the 1990s. Later work adds approximations, additive structure, and PAC-Bayesian learning. Recent empirical-prior methods estimate covariance from historical datasets with heterogeneous observation locations, expanding the role of data in defining the function-space prior itself.
openQuestions: When do learned priors transfer across datasets without becoming overconfident?
How can users compare uncertainty from different kernel and approximation choices?
topic-063-a-framework-for-bayesian-optim.overview: Gaussian processes model uncertainty over functions through a mean and covariance structure. This topic studies regression with input-dependent noise, additive and parametric approximations, robust inference, and data-driven priors. It also examines alternative learning objectives that optimize generalization guarantees rather than marginal likelihood alone.
topic-063-a-framework-for-bayesian-optim.title: Gaussian-Process Regression and Learned Function Priors
topic-063-a-framework-for-bayesian-optim.whyItMatters: A kernel encodes substantial assumptions about how outputs vary together. Useful uncertainty requires those assumptions and the noise model to fit the task, while scalable approximations must preserve the information needed for prediction.
